Base-out transitions for the five reviewed scorecard teams

Source: R/reviewed_base_out.R
reviewed_base_out.Rd

Every offensive event for the team side covered by reviewed_scorecards, with outs and occupied bases before and after the event and runs scored on it. The 179 batting events join one to one with reviewed_scorecards by game_id and event_id. Nine further rows are runner events (stolen bases, a wild pitch, a passed ball and a pickoff) that occur during a plate appearance and are credited to the runner, not the batter.

Usage

reviewed_base_out

Format

A data frame with 188 rows and 15 columns:

game_id

Character MLB game identifier.

team

Character batting team name from MLB.

event_id

Character event identifier. Batting events use the MLB atBatIndex; runner events append the play index, as in "29.2".

at_bat_index

Integer MLB atBatIndex of the plate appearance.

inning

Integer inning number.

event_type

Character MLB event type, such as single or stolen_base_2b.

batting_event

Logical, TRUE for the plate-appearance result.

player

Character credited player: the batter for batting events, the moving runner for runner events.

player_id

Integer MLB identifier of the credited player.

outs_before, outs_after

Integer outs before (0 to 2) and after (0 to 3) the event.

bases_before, bases_after

Integer base mask: 1 for first, 2 for second, 4 for third, added together. Zero after the third out.

runs_scored

Integer runs scored on the event.

verified

Logical, TRUE for all rows; see Details.

Source

MLB Stats API game feeds retrieved November 8, 2026. Feed URLs and SHA-256 hashes are in data-raw/base-out-manifest.json in the source repository, and data-raw/base-out-states.py rebuilds the CSV.

Details

States were replayed from each play's runner movements in the MLB feed. A row is marked verified only when the replayed outs and occupied bases match the feed's own post-play values for that plate appearance, and the replayed runs for each half-inning match the official linescore. All 188 rows passed. Batting events include runner advances on the same play, such as an advance on a throw after a single, following the usual RE24 convention.

Base-out states come from MLB records, not from reading the scorecard. The scorecard reader does not record runner positions.

See also

run_expectancy_fangraphs, calculate_run_impact()

Examples

impact <- calculate_run_impact(reviewed_base_out, run_expectancy_fangraphs)
aggregate(re24 ~ team, impact, sum)
#>                   team   re24
#> 1 Arizona Diamondbacks  0.312
#> 2  Cleveland Guardians -0.149
#> 3      Minnesota Twins -1.149
#> 4        New York Mets  1.851
#> 5  St. Louis Cardinals -3.149
